en: The Sixteenfold Praise of Maṅgala: Om, homage to Samantabhadra, by whom, while dwelling in the forest of merit, many followers of the teaching [were established].
May that Conqueror of Māra protect us, [he whom] Divodāsa and other kings [sought].
May he who indeed subdued the planets in the sacred forest for the sake of protecting the worlds bound by those planets protect us from that fear.
May he who granted liberation protect us—he who ordained the great sages beginning with Kāśyapa and the brahmins beginning with Ānanda for the sake of supreme liberation. (3)
By giving gifts of gold and grain, he protected the distressed brahmin from the constant fear of famine; may that King of the Śākyas protect us. (4)
May he who, having been Maitrakanyaka, overcame his mother’s murderer, and by whom the [demon’s] wheel was cast far away—may that protector of his mother protect us. (5)
May that Supriya protect us— he who, having acquired rains of jewels from his voyage to Badaradvīpa, made the people of Kāśī wealthy with gold.
May he who, having been named Sudhana, revealed a treasure, protect us always from the suffering of poverty—he, the omniscient one. (7)
He entered the royal palace for the purpose of removing diseases such as leprosy;
may that King of Dharma, who constantly protects us from the fear of those various ailments, protect us. 8.
May that Knower of Dharma, who, having become King Kuśa, revealed the supreme majesty of the eighth lunar day (Aṣṭamī) within his own body, protect us.
By means of truthful speech, he established Saudāsa as king in Kāśī;
may that all-knowing one release us from bondage and protect us. 10.
May he who protected the cowherds by manifesting the power of the Goddess, and who removes fear, protect us from the danger of being consumed by fire. 11.
May He who bestowed eyes upon us—the giver of vision—protect us; He who, having granted divine sight to people, placed his own crest-jewel into the water for his mother who had become blind. 12.
He made his son Virūpa, while Chāyā remained exceedingly beautiful, endowed with all auspicious marks; may he, the bestower of everything, protect us always. 13.
May he who, maintaining the lineage, consecrated the one named Sakalānanda upon the throne, and who establishes steadfastness, protect us. 14.
May he who forgave his brother Viṣada when the monks were consuming poison, and who, being wise in the dhāraṇīs, protected them—he, free from poison, may protect us. 15.
May he who set out for Kapila in order to travel to Nepal for the sake of beholding the glorious Svayambhū protect us constantly. (16)
The auspicious sixteen-fold hymn of praise to Śākyasiṃha, extracted from the Bhadrakalpāvadāna, is complete.
